procedure: worker-identified correspondences, deterministically measured. The identification was made by the worker from the federal documentation and the photographs (the drawing's own documented geometry vs the photo's detected structure, cross-checked with VLM-assisted region identification on tight coordinate-grid crops during the annotation session); each identification below records the search window in which the tool measures the position classically (sub-pixel gradient peak). The tool re-measures every position on every run; the identifications (not the positions) are the committed data. The session's full reasoning is recorded in measurements.md.

stillAnnotations.identification: the four distinctive ventilator-sash close pairs and the corner double-line of the south facade, pattern-matched between the drawing's mullion grid and the photo's detected vertical structure: photo pair (740, 760) = drawing vent sash 2 (ventPair2); photo pair (1146, 1166) = sash 3 (ventPair3); photo pair (1627, 1649) = sash 4 (ventPair4); photo pair (1769, 1775) = the SE corner double mullion (corner). The monotonically increasing local scale (0.68 -> 0.81 -> 0.89 photo-px per drawing-px eastward) is the obliquity gradient of the vantage (~24 deg, consistent across the two inter-sash spans); sash 1 is occluded by the elm. Levels: the floor edge (documented MAIN FLOOR EL. 2'-4") is the strongest horizontal edge (~y 1026, flat across the facade - the camera being near the main-floor level); the ceiling edge (documented CEILING EL. 11'-9") is the roof assembly's underside shadow line - selected over the glass-top edge by the documented-ratio consistency test (the glass-top reading would require cos(yaw) > 1 for any real facade view; the shadow-line reading yields the consistent obliquity). The drawing-side feature positions are resolved BY NAME from the tool's own detection of the committed raster (ventPairN = the Nth detected ventilator-sash close pair; corner = the corner double-line) - scale-independent, re-measured on every run.
stillAnnotations.ceilingOmitted: the westernmost sash (photo 740, 760) ceiling points are omitted by the same-sash consistency criterion: the two mullions of one sash must read the same level line within the noise band (1-4 px at sashes 3/4 and the corner); the wide-window readings at sash 2 disagree by 23 px (812 vs 835 - the elm's branches cross the shadow line there), so both are dropped rather than tuned; the floor points at sash 2 are retained (the floor edge is flat and clean)
